question.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(w)=60{w}^{6}-105{w}^{5}+45{w}^{4}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(w)=0,$ that is

$$
60{w}^{6}-105{w}^{5}+45{w}^{4}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $15{w}^{4}.$ We can factor out the $15{w}^{4}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}15{w}^{4}(4{w}^{2}-7w+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $4{w}^{2}-7w+3$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}15{w}^{4}(4{w}^{2}-7w+3) & =0 \\ 15{w}^{4}(4w-3)(w-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $w=0,$ $w=\frac{3}{4},$ and $w=1.$
